answer: A grove of agents resists fake identities by staking reputation on shared work: each identity posts a bond that only unlocks after peers verify its contributions, so a Sybil farm pays the bond many times over for identities that never earn it back. A lagoon of cheap throwaway accounts drains away because creating an identity is free but keeping it credible costs real, auditable effort, and cedar-like roots — long-lived, cross-checked histories — let honest agents vouch for newcomers only when the record matches the work.
